t: Minimum Operations to Achieve At Least K Peaks
o: On a circular array we may increment any element; each increment costs 1. Making index i a peak requires raising it to strictly exceed both neighbors, costing max(0, max(left, right) + 1 - nums[i]). Crucially, adjacent indices cannot both be peaks, and a peak's neighbors are never raised (they are not peaks themselves), so each candidate peak's cost is independent. Thus we must pick an independent set of at least k indices on the cycle minimizing total cost — a classic cycle DP broken by fixing node 0's state. Example 1: one raise makes index 2 a peak (cost 1). Example 2 already has 2 peaks (cost 0). Example 3: n = 3 admits at most 1 peak, so k = 2 is impossible (-1).
k: Cost of making i a peak is max(0, max(nums[i-1], nums[i+1]) + 1 - nums[i]) and is independent across chosen peaks.
Peaks form an independent set on the cycle; at most floor(n/2) peaks are possible, otherwise return -1.
Break the cycle by fixing whether node 0 is a peak, then run a linear DP tracking (previous node peak?, count so far).

a.n: Approach 1: Cycle DP over independent sets with clamped counts
a.i: Precompute cost[i] for every index. Run the DP twice: once assuming node 0 is a peak (then node n-1 must not be), once assuming it is not (node n-1 free). State (previous-is-peak, clamped count up to k) transitions in O(1): skip node i, or take it as a peak if the previous was skipped.
s: If k > n // 2, return -1 (also handle k = 0 -> 0).
Compute cost[i] = max(0, max(prev, next) + 1 - nums[i]) using circular neighbors.
For each fixed state of node 0, DP over i = 1..n-1 with dp[prevPeak][c].
Answer is the minimum over both cases of dp with count >= k.
a.t: O(n·k) — two DP passes over n nodes with k+1 count levels each.
a.sp: O(k) per layer — rolling arrays over the count dimension.

a.n: Approach 2: Brute force over peak sets (small n)
a.i: Enumerate all independent sets of the cycle (bitmasks), compute the total cost of each, and take the minimum among sets of size >= k. Exponential but transparent; good for validating the DP.
s: For each mask over n bits: check no two adjacent set bits (including wrap-around).
If popcount >= k, sum cost[i] over set bits.
Return the minimum total, or -1 if no valid mask has enough bits.
a.t: O(2^n · n) — exponential; only for tiny n.

w: The cycle-broken DP is the intended solution; emphasize why peak costs are independent (neighbors of a peak are never peaks, hence never incremented). Pitfalls: the n = 2 case (both neighbors coincide, at most one peak), the wrap-around adjacency between node 0 and node n-1, and k = 0 returning 0 immediately. Overflow: costs up to ~3e5 summed over 2500 peaks fit in 64-bit. Follow-up: decrements allowed too, or weighted operations per index.
